The most appropriate ground is **Speech or Debate Clause immunity** (U.S. Const. art. I, §6, cl. 1). A senator's floor speech is core legislative activity, so the clause bars this defamation suit outright, whether or not the accusation was false or negligent. The pleading gap is a weaker, secondary ground: a low-level purchasing officer is likely a "public official" under *Rosenblatt v. Baer*, so the complaint would also need to allege actual malice under *New York Times v. Sullivan*.

CONFIDENCE: 80
